analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1227-2134), reviewed against the threat model. The PR is documentation-only, with a date bump and edits to the sandbox setup section (around lines 1035-1186). No code, config, key handling, protocol or enforcement logic changes. The visible text covers drain/stop/restart, status, doctor, models, benchmark, update, beta, fan, login/logout, enroll/unenroll, report and exit codes. It describes existing behavior, and I found no documentation that weakens a stated control.

Security-relevant statements were checked for consistency with the model. Logout and remote revocation (A-008, T-053) and the fan helper requiring explicit sudo (TB-010) read as expected. Update verifies bundle, binary and metallib hashes before replacing the running binary (T-013, T-034). `darkbloom report` redacts logs, keeps automatic upload disabled and drops key identifiers (T-058). Prefix-cache status and the diagnostics around it do not alter the TTL, HMAC or scope claims in T-041. `status` states that the add-on hold line suppresses the Traffic line (TB-012, T-059).

The sandbox setup changes (TB-013, T-061) are mostly outside the supplied head units: the table row at line 1035 is cited only in the patch excerpt, which is truncated. The visible patch shows only the slot-count wording change, to `(your choice)` and chosen counts taken as-is. That is not a security regression on its face. I could not check whether the sandbox installer or hold path enforces the slot bounds, or whether the docs claim anything about installer verification. A next pass should look at the sandbox section (lines ~1035-1190) and the T-061 mitigations if they are referenced. Code paths cited in the docs were not supplied and were not verified.
